name: Cities and Municipalities Competitiveness Index — BARMM
note: DTI’s Cities and Municipalities Competitiveness Index, as published on cmci.dti.gov.ph. A year is the CMCI edition, not the year the underlying data describes (an edition mostly uses the previous year’s data). "overall" is the sum of the pillar scores, each pillar worth up to 20 (four pillars before the 2022 edition, which added Innovation, so those totals are out of 80); "rank" is the rank within "rankCategory" nationally, not within BARMM. Ranks and scores are only comparable inside a category and edition. Provinces carry an overall score and rank only: CMCI derives it as the population- and income-weighted average of its component LGUs’ scores, excluding highly urbanized cities, and publishes no provincial pillars. An LGU missing from a year was not ranked that edition — CMCI participation is voluntary and data-dependent — not scored zero. The 2020 edition ranks only BARMM’s three cities (Cotabato, Lamitan, Marawi); no BARMM municipality or province appears in it. No edition after 2024 is published yet. Sulu, in BARMM until 2024, is left out. "Maguindanao" province rows before its split are under "former"; its towns sit under the province they are in now. The eight Special Geographic Area towns, created in 2024, have never been ranked.
